analysis: overhead-tag to onboard UDP5600 relative visual latency
safety_state: zero propulsion command; operator moved the target by hand; no servo command was sent during this record
timing_method: Use tag 17 pixel-x from the overhead detector because vehicle tags 15/16 were intermittent while the vehicle remained stationary. Its time proxy is host_monotonic_s minus vision_status_age_s. Compare it with host arrival time of the decoded onboard left-eye dark-stem centroid. Search a relative lag while fitting an affine pixel mapping, and independently compare the first retained reversal peak.
limitations: the onboard stem detector was intermittent and the right eye was almost entirely unavailable
the overhead and onboard detections did not observe exactly the same physical image feature
the overhead timestamp is a host-side acquisition proxy, not a hardware exposure timestamp
this is relative visual-chain latency, not exposure-to-control-actuation latency
conclusion: The current onboard stream is near 30 Hz and the motion record suggests a few-tenths-of-a-second relative delay. The uncertainty is too large for fixed MPC delay compensation; retain 0.30 s only as a low-confidence planning prior.
